description:
The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. At Scout AI, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role

We’re looking for a New Grad Software Engineer to join the core software team at Scout AI. You’ll work on the systems Fury runs on: the onboard C++ code and core libraries, the cloud infrastructure that trains and evaluates the model, and the simulation and evals tooling that shows us whether any of it works.

This is a generalist role. Depending on where you’re strongest, you might spend most of your time in onboard C++, in GPU job infrastructure and cloud services, or in simulation and evaluation tooling. Early on you’ll take well-scoped pieces of real systems, work next to senior engineers who review your code, and learn the codebase by changing it. As you get your footing, you’ll be expected to take on bigger pieces.

We use AI coding tools and expect you to as well, but we think of them as a multiplier on skills you already have. You should be able to write, explain, and debug your own code without them.

We’re a startup. You’ll be moving fast, context-switching often, and helping shape the culture and process as we go. It’s a rare chance to come in early and help build the future of defense.

Responsibilities

 - Write and test onboard C++ code and core system libraries, with review from senior engineers

 - Build Python and C++ tools that support ML training and evaluation workloads

 - Help build cloud services for data storage and GPU job scheduling

 - Contribute to simulation and evaluation pipelines, including scenario suites and rendering tools

 - Write automated tests and validation checks that catch problems before a release build ships

 - Read and debug existing code, and help clean up anti-patterns as you learn the system

Qualifications

 - BS or MS in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field, completed or finishing by summer 2027

 - Proficient in C++ or Python (either is fine) from coursework, internships, research, or personal projects

 - Software you have built and debugged yourself, such as an internship project, research code, or a game or robotics project

 - Picks up new tools quickly and asks for help early when stuck

 - Ability to write, debug, and explain complex code independently without relying on AI tools

 - Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

 - Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

 - May be expected to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

Nice to Have

 - Cloud and infrastructure experience (GCS, GPU job scheduling, service deployment)

 - Simulation, game engine, or robotics middleware experience (such as ROS)

 - Edge or embedded hardware familiarity

 - Exposure to training or evaluating ML models

Why Join Scout

 - Work on the world’s most important frontier, ensuring U.S. and allied dominance in the age of intelligent machines

 - Be a core part of a team building the first defense-specific robotic foundation model

 - Collaborate with some of the top engineers in autonomy, AI, and national security

 - See your work deployed on real systems

 - Help define the future of intelligent defense systems

 - Backed by Draper Associates, Booz Allen Ventures, and other top investors

Benefits

 - Competitive Cash Compensation

 - Meaningful equity

 - Premium medical, dental, and vision plans with $0 paycheck contribution

 - 401k with match

 - Competitive PTO and company holiday calendar

 - Catered lunch daily and fully stocked kitchen

 - EV charging

 - Relocation assistance (depending on role eligibility)
